text: Like snow in summer, like rain in harvest,honor for a fool is out of place. [1]
Like the sparrow in its flitting, like the swallow in its flight,a curse uncalled-for never lands. [2]
The whip for the horse, the bridle for the ass,and the rod for the back of fools. [AA]
t[3] Do not answer fools according to their folly,lest you too become like them.
Answer fools according to their folly,lest they become wise in their own eyes.
Those who send messages by a foolcut off their feet; they drink down violence.
t[4] A proverb in the mouth of a foolhangs limp, like crippled legs.
Giving honor to a foolis like entangling a stone in the sling.
A thorn stuck in the hand of a drunkardis a proverb in the mouth of fools.
An archer wounding all who pass byis anyone who hires a drunken fool.
As dogs return to their vomit,so fools repeat their folly. [AB]
You see those who are wise in their own eyes?There is more hope for fools than for them.
t[5] The sluggard says, "There is a lion in the street,a lion in the middle of the square!" [AC]
The door turns on its hingesand sluggards, on their beds.
The sluggard buries a hand in the dish,too weary to lift it to the mouth. [AD]
In their own eyes sluggards are wiserthan seven who answer with good judgment.
Whoever meddles in the quarrel of anotheris one who grabs a passing dog by the ears.
Like a crazed archerscattering firebrands and deadly arrows,
Such are those who deceive their neighbor,and then say, "I was only joking."
t[6] Without wood the fire dies out;without a talebearer strife subsides.
Charcoal for coals, wood for fire—such are the quarrelsome, enkindling strife. [AE]
The words of a talebearer are like dainty morsels:they sink into one's inmost being. [7] [AF]
Like a glazed finish on earthenwareare smooth lips and a wicked heart. [8]
With their lips enemies pretend,but inwardly they maintain deceit;
When they speak graciously, do not trust them, [AG]for seven abominations [9] are in their hearts.
Hatred can be concealed by pretense,but malice will be revealed in the assembly. [10]
Whoever digs a pit falls into it;and a stone comes back upon the one who rolls it. [AH]
The lying tongue is its owner's enemy,and the flattering mouth works ruin.
